# CANDIDATE: VIX_FLOOR_BEAR_ENTRY

**Filed:** 2026-08-24  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Bearish 0DTE put entries suffer from thin premium and failed moves when VIX is low (<15), causing losses that degrade the edge on otherwise winning days. Requiring a minimum VIX of 15 at entry will filter out low-quality bearish setups, preserving the edge on J's winner days (which occurred on moderate-to-high VIX) while reducing losers in choppy low-VIX environments.

## Mechanism

For any bearish setup trigger (BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON, BEARISH_REVERSAL, or any other bearish entry), compute the current VIX from the 5-minute bar's VIX field (available in the SPY 5m dataset). If VIX < 15, suppress the entry. All other entry conditions, exit logic (chart stop, chandelier profit-lock, premium stop, time stop), and position sizing remain unchanged. The filter is applied pre-entry in the risk gate or watcher stage.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The candidate assumes the standard position sizing from risk-rules.md: at $25K+ account equity, 15 contracts are traded for BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON (10 TP + 5 runners). For a $1K paper account, this scales to ~3 contracts (2 TP + 1 runner), realizing approximately 14% of the headline P&L due to the 50% per-trade risk cap.
2. **Sample bias:** The Stage-1 backtest will use the cached OPRA dataset from 2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18 (approx 16 months, n≈?? bearish signals). Selection method: all bars where a bearish setup trigger fires. Overfit risk is low because the filter is a single threshold (VIX>=15) with no look-ahead bias; however, we must verify that the threshold is not tuned to the 5/04 outlier.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward held-out window will be performed as part of Stage-1 grinder; results to be filled after backtest).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (real OPRA fill simulation on the top 3 J days will be run post-backtest; results to be filled).
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: If a bearish winner day has VIX just below 15, the filter could skip a winning trade, turning a winner into a missed opportunity.
   - Max drawdown: In a prolonged low-VIX bear market, the filter may reduce trade frequency, potentially missing a recovery leg and increasing drawdown if the strategy relies on frequent small wins.
   - Blow-up scenario: None introduced; the filter only reduces exposure, so blow-up risk is lower or unchanged.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to compute top-5 days % of P&L.

## Pre-merge gate

- Gym validators: all unit tests in `backtest/tests/` must pass.
- Walk-forward OOS: the grinder's walk-forward module must produce a positive OOS Sharpe ratio (>0) and a WF ratio >=0.70.
- Real-fills check: simulated real OPRA fills on the top 3 J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04) must show no more than -20% deviation from BS-sim P&L for those days.
- No regression on J anchor days: edge_capture must not decrease by more than $50 on any J winner day.

## Confidence

5 / 10 -- The hypothesis is plausible based on VIX's role as a fear gauge, but we lack data to confirm that VIX>=15 improves bearish edge without harming winner days.

## Pre-existing leaderboard impact

This filter_change does not conflict with any existing top-9 candidates in _LEADERBOARD.md because it operates as a pre-entry filter that can be stacked with most strategies. It may complement BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON (not on leaderboard) and any bearish-biased candidate by reducing low-VIX losers. It is orthogonal to exit-change or trigger-change proposals.
